title: Technology Risk Management - Lead Associate

Here, your expertise can help fuel purpose-driven innovation that expands access to homeownership and affordable rental housing across the country. Join Fannie Mae to grow your career and help people find a place to call home. Job Description As a valued colleague on our team, you will provide risk guidance and support assessments that identify and evaluate technology operational risks that could affect our reputation, resilience, security, regulatory obligations, and financial performance. You will collaborate with key stakeholders across the enterprise to understand business and technology objectives, provide effective challenge, and support risk-informed decisions across RCSA, technology assessments, issue management, event management, artificial intelligence, and data analytics. Support Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) activities, including risk identification, control evaluation, evidence review, issue escalation, and residual risk analysis. Support issue management throughout the lifecycle, including root-cause evaluation, remediation planning, milestone monitoring, evidence review, and closure validation. Support operational risk event management by assessing events, analyzing impacts and trends, documenting lessons learned, and monitoring corrective actions. Evaluate risks associated with artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, including responsible use, data, model, security, resilience, and governance considerations. Use data analytics and visualization techniques to identify risk trends, improve monitoring, and communicate actionable insights to stakeholders. Strong interpersonal, collaboration, and influencing skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across technology, business, risk, audit, and compliance teams. Ability to communicate complex risk concepts clearly in written reports, presentations, and discussions with technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Knowledge of artificial intelligence concepts, associated technology and operational risks, and responsible AI governance practices. Proficiency in data analysis, including the ability to interpret datasets, identify trends, and develop actionable risk insights using common analytics and visualization tools. Shows curiosity and adaptability in learning and responsibly applying new technologies, including artificial intelligence, to reimagine how we work. Desired Experiences 5–10 years of experience in technology risk, operational risk, information technology audit, cybersecurity risk, compliance, or a related field. Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience. Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry. Experience with governance, risk, and compliance platforms and data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau. Familiarity with technology and cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST, COBIT, or similar industry standards. In this role, you will drive operational excellence across compliance frameworks, security risk management, third-party assurance, and customer-facing security initiatives while strengthening the processes and technology that support our growing business. This is a hands-on leadership role suited for an experienced GRC professional who can independently manage complex initiatives, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and build scalable, repeatable operations. What you’ll do: Lead and mature Cohere’s GRC program, establishing scalable governance processes, operating procedures, risk management practices, and measurable performance indicators aligned with business objectives. Own the deployment, configuration, and optimization of enterprise GRC platforms, including control mapping, evidence automation, risk registers, continuous monitoring, and compliance reporting. Direct compliance and certification initiatives across HITRUST, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and applicable regulatory requirements, ensuring ongoing audit readiness and effective control execution. Oversee enterprise risk management activities, including risk assessments, remediation tracking, exception management, and the enforcement and reporting of vulnerability remediation SLAs across Engineering, Platform, DevOps, and Data teams. Govern identity and access compliance, including periodic access reviews, privileged access certifications, segregation of duties, and remediation of access control deficiencies. Demonstrated experience deploying and administering enterprise GRC platforms, including implementation, workflow design, control mapping, evidence collection, reporting, and process automation. Familiarity with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 42001, and privacy-related security requirements. Deep understanding of enterprise risk management, including risk registers, control assessments, risk treatment plans, vulnerability remediation SLAs, and formal exception management. Demonstrated project and program management capabilities, including managing concurrent initiatives, developing operational roadmaps, establishing KPIs, and delivering results independently. Demonstrated success developing GRC program maturity models, executive scorecards, and risk-based reporting frameworks. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.  For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster. AI Tech Risk Officer  Adyen combines the agility of a global tech company with the stability of a licensed financial institution. As a Tech Risk Officer focused on AI technology, you will partner with cross-functional teams and regional second-line functions (such as Model risk, Compliance and the DPO office) to ensure safe, secure, and resilient implementation of autonomous AI architectures and regulatory requirements. The Tech Risk team, part of the second line risk function ensures that risk management practices are applied across Adyen’s technological environments, teams and initiatives. This continuous task requires a close and supporting relationship with tech teams in the first line, in order to understand changes in the tech landscape but also to guide them in relation to risk mitigations.  In this role, you will focus on the unique security and architectural risks associated with building, deploying, and monitoring autonomous AI agents, working closely with first-line engineering teams to embed risk mitigation into technical design. You will be part of building technology, challenging design and execution through constructive and positive conversations. Realize better outcomes together.  The ideal candidate is a risk or tech professional with hands-on experience evaluating and managing risks arising from the implementation of AI solutions, software architecture for agentic systems and the underlying tech stack. You have a technical background that enables you to evaluate agentic workflows, models safety, and integration points, advancing our second-line risk framework to support safe AI innovation at scale. Both security as well as IT-resilience experience is welcome.  What you will do  Evaluate technology threats and risks  across diverse AI developments in the industry, internal projects and assets, advising stakeholders and ensuring risk mitigation actions are implemented.  Collaborate closely with leadership and build an internal network to ensure the domain remains represented in business activities, contributing to decision making.  Drive the second line risk oversight for AI and general Technology risks, including KRI design, risk monitoring and reporting.  Collaborate with other Risk domains, in order to incorporate AI Tech risks into Adyen’s risk profile, ensuring those are considered when evaluating company objectives.  Collaborate with or advise other second-line teams (typically Regulatory, Compliance and Privacy) in the implementation of AI Governance requirements in Adyen’s tech environments, as well as engage with local auditors or external partners (externally) as a trusted point of contact for the specific risk domain, globally.  Engage with various regulators to provide clarity on Adyen’s IT Resilience and excellence landscape. Who you are You have at least 5+ years experience within a risk management function, with 2 years of demonstrated experience guiding AI risk mitigations, AI Governance or AI Cyber Security.   Demonstrated experience evaluating technology risks, Security best practices and associated industry and regulatory frameworks.  You feel comfortable explaining risks associated with IT environments to engineers but also to business stakeholders.  You have a solid understanding of commonly used AI technology stack (hardware, software, network and systems, on-prem or cloud solutions), at the level required to identify risks or weaknesses and recommend tangible actions, design metrics to enable risk monitoring and oversight.  You are innovative, flexible with strong problem-solving capabilities and able to define effective processes, when possible scaling manual processes via automation.  Available to work from our New York or San Francisco office and travel to other offices periodically. title: Principal Security Engineer, AI Governance
description: What You Can Expect As a Senior Security Engineer on Zoom's Enterprise Security team, you will own the AI Governance program end to end, defining the technical standards and risk posture that determine how Zoom adopts AI safely and at scale. On any given day, you will be assessing emerging AI use cases, building security frameworks for GenAI and agentic systems, and serving as the trusted technical voice on AI security for engineering and enterprise stakeholders across four critical domains. This is a hands-on, highly autonomous role that calls for real depth in both AI/ML systems and security engineering; candidates without working familiarity with how modern AI introduces security risk will not be set up for success here. You will work as part of a globally distributed, multi-domain security engineering team, collaborating closely with colleagues across time zones and contributing across adjacent security domains beyond AI. About the Team Zoom's Enterprise Security team is the engineering foundation behind how the company identifies, contains, and gets ahead of risk across its most critical systems. Working across AI, data, network, endpoint, and cloud security, the team builds the controls, standards, and architectures that let Zoom move quickly without creating unacceptable exposure. As Zoom deepens its investment in AI across Zoom Workplace and its broader platform, this team's work is increasingly central to how the company grows responsibly. Responsibilities Own the AI governance risk register and end-to-end assessment methodology across four domains (GenAI, Agentic AI, Shadow AI/Local AI, and AI Gateway/MCP); conduct and review risk evaluations using Likelihood x Impact scoring and drive remediation with owning engineering teams. Identify and prioritize security gaps in GenAI deployments including prompt injection, data leakage, model misuse, and insecure output handling; define monitoring and guardrail requirements for agentic systems operating with significant autonomy and tool access. Lead the Shadow AI governance strategy end to end, from quantifying risk exposure to recommending and operationalizing detection and enforcement controls across the enterprise. Set the security bar for AI gateway and Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementations, including secure configuration, access control frameworks, and governance coverage. Architect reference security patterns for AI adoption (AI gateways, MCP servers, agent frameworks, LLM integrations) and serve as design authority in AI-related architecture reviews; translate the AI Governance Risk Charter into a concrete roadmap of technical requirements and measurable outcomes. Drive evaluations of AI security tooling (AI gateways, CASB/SWG, agentic monitoring, MCP governance solutions), including POC design, cost-benefit analysis, and leadership recommendations; author and maintain security standards and policy for AI adoption. Lead security architecture reviews and risk assessments across adjacent domains including Network, Endpoint, Cloud, and Data Security; contribute to incident response, detection engineering, and purple team exercises as shared team functions. Serve as the primary technical partner to AI/ML, engineering, and enterprise teams; lead cross-functional working groups, mentor engineers on risk analysis and documentation quality, and deliver clear reporting on AI risk posture and forecasted challenges to leadership. What We're Looking For 10+ years of security engineering or cybersecurity experience, including end-to-end ownership of a security domain or program, with a track record of driving risk assessment, prioritization, and remediation across cross-functional teams. Solid working knowledge of modern AI/ML systems and the security risks they introduce (LLMs, generative AI, agentic systems); direct experience securing GenAI or LLM-based applications in an enterprise environment is a strong differentiator. Understanding of AI gateways, Model Context Protocol (MCP), CASB/SWG, or DLP tooling, and a working understanding of shadow AI detection and governance strategies. Working knowledge across core security domains (network, endpoint, cloud, and data security) sufficient to independently lead architecture reviews and risk assessments outside of AI. Experience designing security reference architectures or serving as a design authority in complex, cross-functional technical environments; threat modeling experience applied to AI or novel technology stacks is a plus. Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, communicate risk clearly in writing and verbally, and drive alignment across engineering, product, and enterprise teams without direct authority. Comfort operating in a globally distributed team with regular overlap with US Pacific hours; ability to work with high autonomy and produce clear, actionable risk documentation for leadership audiences. We achieve this through the implementation of comprehensive policies, processes, controls, and metrics that ensure compliance with global regulations. The Impact: S&P Global is seeking an Director, Information Governance and Records Management to lead, mature, and scale the enterprise-wide information governance and records management program across its global data and analytics business, with supporting responsibility for data governance, privacy by design, and AI governance. This role owns the strategy, policies, standards, and controls that govern the full lifecycle of S&P Global’s business records and information, from creation and capture through classification, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition. The Director will ensure that records and information management practices align with S&P Global’s Information Governance Policy framework, Privacy Program, and evolving legal, regulatory, and recordkeeping obligations across jurisdictions. The position plays a critical leadership role in operationalizing the enterprise records retention schedule, strengthening information classification compliance, and reducing over-retention risk, while supporting a risk-based data management and governance model, privacy by design, and responsible AI practices that underpin S&P Global’s delivery of data-driven products and services, including analytics, ratings, market intelligence, and entity-based data solutions. S&P Global’s business model—focused on delivering data, analytics, and insight to global markets—requires robust governance over data sourcing, processing, retention, and usage to ensure trust, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience. What’s in it for you: In this role, you will: Collaborate with senior and executive stakeholders globally. Act as a senior advisor to stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Technology, and business divisions. Lead cross-functional governance forums to drive alignment and accountability for data governance activities. Be an integral part of building and maturing the global Information Governance and Records Management program, working alongside executive leadership to drive our team forward. Responsibilities: The Associate Director, Information Governance and Records Management will be responsible for: Information Governance & Records Management Leadership Lead the strategy, design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the enterprise Information Governance and Records Management program, covering the full information lifecycle (creation, capture, use, storage, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition) across paper and electronic records. Own and maintain core policies and standards, including: Information Governance Policy Information Classification Standard Records Retention Schedule Legal Hold and Defensible Disposition procedures Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, internal risk frameworks, and international standards. Maintain and periodically refresh the global Records Retention Schedule, conducting legal and regulatory retention research across jurisdictions and securing business sign-off on record classes and retention periods. Drive operational adoption of retention requirements across business divisions and enterprise systems, including records inventories, system-level retention configuration, and coordinated defensible disposition of records and data that have met their retention periods. Partner with Legal and eDiscovery teams to manage the legal hold process and ensure holds override routine disposition. Develop and deliver information governance and records management training, communications, and a network of divisional records coordinators. Data Classification & Information Handling Establish and oversee enterprise-wide data classification frameworks and compliance monitoring. Partner with Information Security and technology teams to ensure appropriate controls for data access, storage, and protection. Implement and track metrics to measure classification compliance and data handling effectiveness. title: Director, SOX Compliance & Internal Controls
description: From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven. About Us Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.  Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.  During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites. About the Role Fivetran is building a SOX Compliance function from the ground up. Reporting directly to the Chief Accounting Officer (CAO), the Director, SOX Compliance & Internal Controls will design and stand up Fivetran’s internal controls program using the COSO framework. This will include risk and control matrices (RCMs), narratives, and test plans for both business process controls and IT application controls/IT general controls (ITACs/ITGCs). The individual will own the relationship with third-party control-testing providers and the external audit team (KPMG) as the company moves through its SOX readiness and 404(a) compliance. This is a highly visible, build-phase mandate. You will have significant latitude and accountability to shape the control environment, tooling, and governance model that Fivetran will operate on. You will partner closely with Accounting, India CoE, FP&A, Legal, HROps, Revenue, IT/Engineering, Security, and every control owner across the business. This is a full-time, hybrid position based out of our Oakland, CA office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including one day in the office each week to connect and build as a team.  What You’ll Do SOX Program Build & Governance ▪ Design, build, and lead Fivetran’s end-to-end SOX 404 compliance program in accordance with the COSO 2013 framework and 404(b) integrated audit standards. ▪ Lead the risk assessment and scoping process (significant accounts, processes, and locations) in partnership with the external auditors. ▪ Build and maintain the company’s risk and control matrices (RCMs), process narratives, and flowcharts across key financial processes, including order-to-cash/revenue, procure-to-pay, payroll and equity compensation, treasury, financial close and reporting, tax and entity-level controls. ▪ Design and document control activities (preventive and detective, manual and automated) that are efficient, right-sized, and audit-ready. ▪ Build a SOX/GRC workflow tool using AI to manage controls, testing, issues, and evidence. ITGC / ITAC & IT Risk ▪ Partner with Engineering, IT, and Security to design and test IT general controls (access management, change management, computer operations/backups) and IT application controls (automated controls, interfaces, system-generated reports/IPE) across in-scope systems (NetSuite, Coupa, Salesforce CRM, Workday, data warehouse, AI-agents built using frontier AI models and other SaaS solutions). ▪ Build segregation-of-duties (SoD) analysis and monitoring across key financial systems. ▪ Serve as the trusted advisor to technical teams on control design for new systems, integrations, and process changes, including evaluating SOC 1/SOC 2 reports from key vendors and determining reliance. Testing, Third Parties & External Audit ▪ Develop test plans and testing strategies (design and operating effectiveness) for all in-scope controls, both business-process and ITGC/ITAC. ▪ Engage, manage, and oversee third-party co-source/outsource providers performing SOX control testing, including scoping the engagement, setting standards for workpaper quality, and reviewing their results before sharing with external auditors. ▪ Own the primary relationship with KPMG (external auditor) fo

title: Manager – GenAI Strategy & Architecture
description: Who/What is Artefact? Artefact is a next-generation strategy and data consulting firm dedicated to transforming organizations through data and AI. We combine the rigor of top-tier strategy consulting with deep expertise in data, digital, and analytics to help clients achieve tangible business impact. With 1,800+ consultants, data scientists, and engineers across 23 countries, we work with global leaders such as Samsung, L’Oréal, Orange, and Sanofi. Our Zurich office is at the heart of Artefact’s growth, advising clients on their most pressing strategic challenges — from AI strategy and governance to digital transformation roadmaps and new business model design.   The role:   We are looking for a Manager who leads strategy and architecture projects focused on GenAI solutions. You will own the design of architectures and solutions end to end, balancing business value, technology choices and economics across every dimension of the decision. You will lead development teams, present solutions to C-level stakeholders and run technical and strategic workshops independently.   Key responsibilities: Project and programme leadership Lead strategy and architecture projects on GenAI, from scoping and business case through to solution design and rollout oversight. Own project plans, budgets, risks and quality, ensuring delivery against client objectives. Shape proposals, estimates and demos, and identify follow-on opportunities with clients. GenAI architecture and solution design Design GenAI architectures and solutions: RAG, agentic systems, multi-agent orchestration, MCP and A2A integration, copilots and assistants. Select and combine cloud-native AI services (e.g. Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, Vertex AI, Bedrock, Databricks) with third-party and custom components. Apply GenAI to support functions such as HR, Procurement, Legal, Finance and IT, redesigning processes and operating models around the new solutions. Cross-dimension optimization and trade-offs Orchestrate decisions across make, buy and customization options, weighing capex against opex and total cost of ownership. Assess the impact of tool and architecture choices on vendor lock-in, performance, latency, scalability, security and compliance. Translate these trade-offs into clear recommendations that business and IT leaders can act on. Team and stakeholder leadership Guide development teams technically: set the architecture, review solutions and unblock delivery. Present solutions and recommendations to C-level audiences. Run technical and strategic workshops independently, from discovery to design and prioritization. Coach and develop consultants and architects in the team. Requirements: At least 8 years of professional experience in IT. At least 3 years on AI/GenAI architecture and solution design projects. Prior hands-on background as an engineer or developer. Proven experience applying GenAI to support functions (HR, Procurement, Legal, Finance or IT). Consulting experience, ideally in strategy consulting, combined with experience at a system integrator or delivery firm. Track record of managing projects and leading teams, including development teams. Experience presenting to C-level stakeholders and running workshops independently. Excellent written and spoken English. Technical and functional skills: GenAI architectures: RAG, agentic and multi-agent patterns, LLMOps, model evaluation, guardrails and responsible AI. Agent protocols and copilots: MCP, A2A, Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio, custom assistants and their integration with enterprise systems. Cloud AI platforms: Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI, Bedrock, Databricks and the native data and AI services of Azure, AWS and GCP. Architecture trade-offs: make vs buy vs customize, capex vs opex, TCO, lock-in, performance, latency, scalability, security and compliance. Support functions: processes and operating models in HR, Procurement, Legal, Finance and IT, and how GenAI changes them. Delivery leadership: agile methods, technical team guidance, solution review, programme governance. Business: business cases, value tracking, and the ability to translate technical choices into economic impact for executives. Nice to have: German not strictly required. Cloud or AI certifications (e.g. Azure AI Engineer, Azure Solutions Architect, AWS Machine Learning). What we offer: A leadership role bridging strategy, architecture and GenAI delivery, with direct impact on client decisions. International projects on GenAI, agentic systems and support function transformation. A growth path towards senior programme and practice leadership roles. Location and working model: (Hybrid) Zurich or Lausanne. Highly competitive compensation package.   This position is based in Zürich . Don’t worry if you don’t meet all the criteria! We value motivation, pragmatic problem-solving, and potential above all else. We’d love to hear from you and learn more about your passion for driving the AI revolution.   Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow
